kapak.alt: Seating a child with hearing loss

youtube.baslik: Is the front-row center seat best for a child with hearing loss? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: Sitting near the teacher keeps the child in the zone where direct sound is stronger than reflected sound; the distance where direct and reflected sound are equal is called the critical distance. But the front center seat is not always best; the child should be able to turn slightly to see classmates too. In a child with unilateral or asymmetric loss, the better ear should face the teacher and the class; a U-shaped seating layout makes it easier to see the faces of both the teacher and classmates.
youtube.kapanis_metni: Follow AIHEAR Audiology Academy for more quick facts.
